strengths: DFT is simple and practical: probability-weighted token updates require no additional reward model, reference model, or online sampling in the supervised setting.

Table 1 reports substantial improvements over SFT across five models and five mathematics benchmarks. Average accuracy rises from 18.01 to 31.58 for Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B and from 23.62 to 37.15 for Qwen2.5-Math-7B.

The evaluation includes a relevant concurrent baseline, iw-SFT, learning curves, and learning-rate and batch-size sweeps. The latter provide useful evidence that the improvements are not solely due to the default SFT hyperparameters.
weaknesses: The central theoretical explanation confuses the variance of a hypothetical on-policy importance-sampling estimator with that of actual supervised training. SFT samples demonstrations directly and never uses the sparse estimator in Equation 5. Its softmax cross-entropy gradient with respect to logits is bounded. The change-of-measure identity therefore does not establish that SFT suffers from unbounded gradient variance or that this causes poor generalization. Calling the exact importance correction 'biased' is also misleading.

The implemented token-level objective does not follow directly from the sequence-level argument: replacing trajectory probabilities with individual token probabilities changes the objective and leaves expert-prefix conditioning intact. The claimed equivalence to uniformly rewarded trajectory RL requires further justification. Equation 7 also places example-dependent weighting outside an expectation, while Equation 8 has a sign and indexing inconsistency.

The novelty discussion misses a direct connection to established classification losses. With stop-gradient weighting, -sg(p) log(p) has gradient -∇p, exactly matching 1-p and, up to scaling, categorical mean absolute error. Positioning against these losses and generalized cross-entropy is necessary to establish what is novel beyond their application to LLM fine-tuning.

The offline RL data description is internally inconsistent: 10,000 questions with four responses each yield at most 40,000 responses, yet the paper reports retaining approximately 140,000 correct examples. Online training budgets, rollout costs, and several algorithm-specific settings are also unspecified, preventing a reliable assessment of the claimed superiority and efficiency over PPO/GRPO.

Evidence for generalization and the proposed mechanism remains incomplete. All experiments use mathematics data, no training–evaluation overlap audit is reported, and there are no independent training seeds or confidence intervals. Sixteen decoding runs do not measure training variability. Token-probability histograms alone cannot establish that suppressing grammatical tokens causes better reasoning or that gradient variance is reduced.

Reporting inconsistencies reduce confidence and reproducibility. Several improvement ratios in Section 4.1.2 do not match Table 1; the SFT and DFT supervised results change between Tables 1 and 3 without explanation; and the promised code link is absent. Although the empirical gains are promising, these issues and the unsupported central theoretical claims require substantial revision.

strengths: DFT is simple and inexpensive: it weights each token’s cross-entropy gradient by its detached probability, requiring neither a reference model nor additional rollouts in the supervised setting.

Table 1 reports substantial improvements over SFT across five models and five mathematical benchmarks. Average accuracy increases from 18.01 to 31.58 for Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B and from 23.62 to 37.15 for Qwen2.5-Math-7B.

The evaluation includes a relevant concurrent baseline, iw-SFT, training curves, and learning-rate and batch-size sweeps. These sweeps provide evidence that the gains are not simply due to one poorly chosen SFT learning rate.
weaknesses: The central theoretical explanation is unsupported. Equations 5–6 rewrite an expectation using importance sampling, but ordinary SFT samples demonstrations directly, not model trajectories with sparse exact-match rewards. High variance of this hypothetical on-policy estimator does not establish high variance or poor generalization of the actual SFT estimator. For softmax cross-entropy, the logit gradient is p minus the target indicator and remains bounded even when the target probability approaches zero. Calling the exact importance-weighted identity 'biased' is also misleading.

The practical token-level method does not follow from the trajectory-level derivation. Replacing whole-response probabilities with conditional token probabilities changes the objective and leaves training under expert prefixes; it is not merely a numerical stabilization preserving the claimed RL equivalence. Equation 7 also places a sample-dependent factor outside the expectation, and Equation 8 has a sign inconsistent with Equation 9.

Novelty is insufficiently positioned against existing robust classification objectives. Since -sg(p)∇log(p) = -∇p, the proposed update is gradient-equivalent to minimizing 1-p, proportional to one-hot classification MAE. The paper should discuss this connection and distinguish its LLM application and findings from novelty of the loss itself.

The offline experiment contains a material data-accounting contradiction: 10,000 questions with four responses each yield at most 40,000 responses, yet Section 4.2 reports approximately 140,000 retained correct examples and 100,000 preference pairs without explaining augmentation or resampling. Training and rollout budgets are insufficiently specified to substantiate efficiency or superiority over online RL.

Experimental uncertainty and reproducibility remain incomplete. Sixteen decoding runs do not measure training-seed variability, and no confidence intervals are reported. SFT and DFT results differ between Tables 1 and 3 without a clear explanation. Exact prompts, checkpoint-selection rules, and benchmark-overlap checks are not sufficiently documented.

The interpretation exceeds the evidence. Math-only evaluation does not establish broad improvements to SFT generalization, and aggregate token histograms do not demonstrate that suppressing grammatical tokens causes better reasoning. DFT also trails iw-SFT on Qwen2.5-Math-7B average accuracy, 37.15 versus 39.60. The promising empirical results do not resolve the central theoretical and evaluation problems sufficiently for acceptance.

strengths: DFT is simple and inexpensive: multiplying token-level cross-entropy by the detached target probability requires no additional model, rollout, or reward annotation in the standard supervised setting.

The reported mathematical reasoning gains are substantial and consistent across five base models. For Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B, average accuracy increases from 18.01 with SFT to 31.58 with DFT; similar improvements occur across other model families.

The evaluation extends to code generation, multimodal reasoning, rejection-sampled training data, and LoRA. Appendix A.8 includes meaningful learning-rate and batch-size sweeps, providing evidence that the gains are not simply due to one poor SFT configuration.
Comparison with concurrent iw-SFT provides useful positioning: DFT wins on four of five model-level averages, although iw-SFT wins on Qwen2.5-Math-7B.
weaknesses: The central theoretical explanation is not established. Equation 5 is an exact change-of-measure identity; its importance weight does not make the original SFT estimator biased or inherently unstable. For softmax logits, the cross-entropy gradient is p minus the one-hot target, which remains bounded even when the target probability approaches zero. Thus, the displayed 1/p factor alone does not establish exploding gradients, overfitting, or poor generalization. No generalization result or direct gradient-stability measurements substantiate this causal claim.

The sequence-level derivation does not justify the implemented token-level objective. Maximizing the probability of an entire expert trajectory differs fundamentally from maximizing the sum of target-token probabilities under expert prefixes. Replacing trajectory weights with token weights changes the objective and does not correct the prefix-distribution mismatch. Consequently, the claimed equivalence to uniformly rewarded on-policy trajectory learning does not follow for Equation 9.

Novelty needs substantially stronger positioning. As Appendix A.4 acknowledges, the implemented gradient is exactly that of negative target probability, which is also equivalent up to scaling and an additive constant to multiclass mean absolute error against one-hot labels. The paper should address this established loss family and compare experimentally with closely related demonstration-learning objectives such as GOLD and MixCE, rather than relying primarily on vanilla SFT.

The proposed mechanism remains speculative. Training-token histograms cannot demonstrate reduced overfitting, better calibration, or preferential learning of semantic content. Direct noise-controlled experiments, held-out calibration measurements, and alternative confidence-weighting baselines would help distinguish the proposed explanation from robust fitting or preservation of pretrained behavior.

The claimed advantage over online RL lacks a sufficiently controlled comparison. Training budgets, total generated tokens, compute costs, baseline tuning, and important PPO/GRPO settings are insufficiently documented. The results support superiority over the reported configurations, but not the broader efficiency and scalability claims.

Experimental uncertainty and reporting need improvement. Sixteen decoding runs do not measure training-seed variability, and no confidence intervals are provided for small benchmarks or modest multimodal gains. Equation 8 omits the negative sign, several improvement ratios disagree with the tables, and Table 6 reports a different standard-setting DFT result without explaining the change. These issues reduce confidence in the presentation despite the promising empirical results.

strengths: DFT is simple and inexpensive: multiplying token cross-entropy by the detached target-token probability requires no additional model or online sampling in the demonstration-only setting.

The reported mathematical reasoning gains are substantial across five models. For example, Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B improves from 18.01 average accuracy with SFT to 31.58 with DFT, and DeepSeekMath-7B improves from 9.82 to 18.15.

Experiments extend to code generation, multimodal reasoning, verified model-generated demonstrations, and LoRA. Appendix A.8 includes learning-rate and batch-size sweeps that provide useful evidence against a simple hyperparameter explanation.
weaknesses: The central theoretical explanation is unsupported. Equations 5–6 are a change-of-measure identity, not evidence that ordinary demonstration-based SFT suffers from unstable importance-sampling estimates. For softmax logits, the cross-entropy gradient is p minus the target indicator and remains bounded as the target probability approaches zero. The displayed 1/p factor alone therefore does not establish exploding gradients, biased optimization, or poor generalization.

The RL equivalence needs substantial qualification. Treating the effective reward 1[y=y*]/p_theta(y|x) as a conventional reward ignores its parameter dependence; differentiating its expected value also introduces reward-derivative terms. A detached gradient correspondence is possible, but does not establish the claimed equivalence of optimization objectives.

The transition from sequence weighting to token weighting changes the objective rather than merely resolving numerical instability. Equation 9 maximizes individual target-token probabilities under fixed expert prefixes; it is not the sequence-level exact-match policy objective derived earlier. The claimed uniform trajectory reward and analogy to verification-based RL consequently do not directly justify the implemented method. Equation 8 also omits the negative sign required by the surrounding loss definitions.

Novelty is insufficiently established against closely related objectives. Appendix A.4 correctly identifies the gradient as that of negative target probability, which is also proportional to multiclass mean absolute error for one-hot labels. The paper needs clearer positioning against this loss family and direct comparisons with related demonstration-weighting methods such as GOLD and MixCE, rather than primarily contrasting DFT with ordinary SFT and general RL algorithms.

The experiments support improved benchmark accuracy more convincingly than the proposed mechanism. There are no direct gradient-stability measurements, controlled noise experiments, or quantitative calibration analyses. Figure 2's aggregate training-token histogram cannot establish that suppressing grammatical tokens causes better generalization or that the method improves calibration.

Evaluation uncertainty and RL comparison details remain incomplete. Sixteen decoding runs do not replace independent training seeds or confidence intervals, particularly for small benchmarks and modest multimodal gains. The online RL comparisons lack sufficiently documented training budgets, tuning, and measured computational costs to establish the claimed efficiency advantage.

Several reporting inconsistencies reduce confidence in the presentation: Section 4.1.2 gives gain ratios inconsistent with Table 1; Appendix A.7 labels a base-to-DFT gain as an SFT-to-DFT gain; and Table 6 reports an unexplained different demonstration-only DFT result from Table 1. These issues require reconciliation. Overall, the promising empirical results do not yet overcome the central theoretical and positioning weaknesses.

strengths: DFT is simple and inexpensive: multiplying each token’s cross-entropy by its detached probability requires no additional model, rollout, or reward annotation in the standard SFT setting.

The empirical improvements over SFT are substantial across five math models. For example, average accuracy increases from 18.01 to 31.58 for Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B and from 23.62 to 37.15 for Qwen2.5-Math-7B.
Experiments extend to code generation, multimodal reasoning, higher-quality reasoning demonstrations, and LoRA, providing useful evidence of practical applicability.

Appendix A.8 includes learning-rate and batch-size sweeps, strengthening the evidence that the main gains are not simply caused by one poor SFT hyperparameter choice. The comparison with concurrent iw-SFT is also valuable.
weaknesses: The central theoretical explanation is not established. Equation 5 is an exact change-of-measure identity; its inverse-probability factor does not make the original supervised gradient biased or inherently unstable. For softmax logits, the cross-entropy gradient is p minus the target indicator and remains bounded as target probability approaches zero. The paper therefore cannot infer exploding SFT updates or poor generalization merely from the displayed 1/p factor. No gradient measurements or generalization analysis substantiate this causal claim.

The sequence-to-token transition changes the objective rather than merely improving numerical stability. Maximizing a reference sequence’s probability differs from maximizing the sum of token probabilities under teacher-forced prefixes. Consequently, the claimed equivalence between the implemented token-level method and uniform-reward trajectory RL does not follow from the derivation.

Novelty relative to existing probability-weighted learning is insufficiently resolved. Appendix A.4 establishes that the implemented update is simply the gradient of negative target-token probability, closely connecting it to established linear-probability/MAE objectives. GOLD and MixCE are cited but not evaluated, and the discussion does not establish precisely how DFT’s implemented update differs from their related weighting mechanisms.

The generalization and mechanism claims exceed the evidence. Benchmark improvements are encouraging, but there is no explicit distribution-shift protocol or reported train–test overlap audit. Figure 2’s training-set probability histograms do not establish reduced overfitting, improved calibration, or a causal benefit from suppressing grammatical tokens.

The RL comparison lacks sufficient controls to support broad superiority or efficiency claims. Training budgets, rollout-token costs, stopping criteria, and baseline tuning are not adequately documented, and no wall-clock or memory measurements are provided. The experiment uses only one small model. DFT also trails iw-SFT on Qwen2.5-Math-7B, including average accuracy of 37.15 versus 39.60.

Uncertainty and reproducibility reporting are incomplete. Sixteen decoding runs do not measure training-seed variability, and no confidence intervals are reported, which matters especially for small benchmarks and modest multimodal gains.
